q: There are at least ____ different organic compounds currently on the planet and every one of them is unique in its chemical structure and specific properties.
e: The text states there are at least ten million different organic compounds currently on the planet.

q: The ____ atom is central to all organic compounds.
e: Carbon is the central atom to all organic compounds.

q: Organic compounds contain carbon and hydrogen in which there is at least one ____ or C-H bond and sometimes a few other elements such as oxygen, nitrogen, sulphur, phosphorus and the halogens.
e: Organic compounds must contain at least one C-C or C-H bond.

q: The bonding patterns of carbon with its valence of ____ form single, double and triple bonds.
e: Carbon has a valence of four, allowing it to form single, double, and triple bonds.

q: Carbon forms a large number of compounds with hydrogen which are collectively called ____.
e: Compounds consisting entirely of carbon and hydrogen are collectively called hydrocarbons.

q: Hydrocarbons are compounds in which carbon and hydrogen atoms bonded to each other by ____ bonds.
e: The bonds between carbon and hydrogen atoms in hydrocarbons are covalent.

q: The hydrocarbon compounds that contain only single bonds are called saturated hydrocarbons, and are classified as ____.
e: Saturated hydrocarbons containing only single bonds are classified as alkanes.

q: Those that contain double or triple bonds are called ____ hydrocarbons which include alkenes, alkynes and aromatic compounds.
e: Hydrocarbons with double or triple bonds are termed unsaturated.

q: The ____ formula is used to represent the families of organic compounds.
e: A general formula represents the composition of any member of an entire class of compounds.

q: The ____ formula of an organic compound is the actual number of atoms of each element present in a molecule.
e: The molecular formula gives the actual number of atoms of each element in a molecule.

q: A ____ structural formula (graphic formula or displayed formula) shows every bond and atom in what order atoms are attached, but does not portray accurately the three-dimensional geometry of the molecule.
e: A full structural formula shows every bond and atom in the molecule.

q: A ____ structural formula is a more compact way of drawing the structural formula of a molecule.
e: A condensed structural formula omits certain bonds and groups atoms together for compactness.

q: Organic compounds are classified according to the different types of ____ groups.
e: Functional groups determine the chemical properties and classification of organic compounds.

q: An alkane is a compound that lacks ____ groups.
e: Alkanes lack functional groups, containing only carbon and hydrogen with single bonds.

q: The functional group in an alkene is a carbon-carbon ____ bond.
e: The functional group characteristic of alkenes is a carbon-carbon double bond.

q: The functional group in an alkyne is a carbon-carbon ____ bond.
e: The functional group characteristic of alkynes is a carbon-carbon triple bond.

q: A functional group is an atom or a group or atoms that determine the ____ properties of a compound.
e: Functional groups represent potential reaction sites and determine the chemical properties of a compound.

q: An alcohol is an organic compound with a ____ (-OH) functional group attached to a carbon atom.
e: Alcohols are characterized by the presence of a hydroxyl (-OH) functional group.

q: Alcohols can often be represented by the general formula ROH, where R is an ____ group.
e: In the general formula ROH, R represents an alkyl group.

q: A ____ series is a group of organic compounds, usually listed in order of increasing size, that have the same functional group and similar structure.
e: A homologous series is a family of compounds with the same functional group and similar structures.

q: In a homologous series, all the compounds differ only by the number of ____ units in the main carbon chain.
e: Consecutive members of a homologous series differ by a $CH_2$ unit.

q: In a homologous series, all the compounds fit the same ____ formula.
e: All members of a homologous series can be represented by the same general formula.

q: As the chain gets longer, the compounds show a ____ change in properties.
e: Physical properties show a gradual change as the carbon chain gets longer in a homologous series.

q: The alkanes are the simplest family of organic compounds and are referred to as the '____ hydrocarbons'.
e: Alkanes are called saturated hydrocarbons because they contain only single covalent bonds.

q: Alkanes contain only ____ and hydrogen atoms.
e: Alkanes are hydrocarbons, meaning they consist exclusively of carbon and hydrogen.

q: Every carbon in an alkane has a ____ environment and is bonded to four other atoms.
e: The four single bonds around each carbon atom in an alkane create a tetrahedral geometry.

q: Alkanes form a homologous series, with the general formula ____ where n is a number equal to or greater than 1.
e: The general formula for non-cyclic alkanes is $C_nH_{2n+2}$.

q: The representative alkane given here is ____, $C_2H_6$.
e: Ethane is the second member of the alkane homologous series with the formula $C_2H_6$.

q: The root name for an organic compound indicates the number of carbon atoms in the ____ continuous chain of carbon atoms.
e: IUPAC nomenclature requires identifying the longest continuous carbon chain to determine the root name.

q: The alkyl groups (also known as alkyl radicals) are derived from the corresponding alkanes by the removal of a ____ atom.
e: An alkyl group is formed when one hydrogen atom is removed from an alkane.

q: Alkyl groups are represented generally as R-, where R is ____.
e: The general formula for an alkyl group is $C_nH_{2n+1}$.

q: In the IUPAC system, identify and name the ____ carbon chain.
e: The first rule of IUPAC naming is to identify the longest carbon chain.

q: Number the C atoms in this longest chain beginning at the end ____ the first branching.
e: Carbon atoms are numbered starting from the end nearest to the first substituent or branch.

q: Assign the name and position number to each ____.
e: Substituents are groups attached to the main carbon chain and must be named and numbered.

q: Arrange the substituents in ____ order.
e: When multiple different substituents are present, they are listed in alphabetical order.

q: Use the appropriate ____ to group like substituents: di, tri, tetra, penta, and so on.
e: Prefixes like di, tri, and tetra indicate the number of identical substituents.

q: Do not consider these prefixes when ____ attached groups.
e: Prefixes such as di- and tri- are ignored when alphabetizing substituent names.

q: Write the name as a ____ word.
e: The final IUPAC name is written as a single word, using hyphens and commas appropriately.

q: Two or more compounds with the same molecular formula but different arrangements of atoms and have different properties from each other are called ____.
e: Isomers share the same molecular formula but differ in the arrangement of atoms.

q: Straight chain and branched-chain isomers are examples of ____ isomers that differ in the order in which the atoms are bonded together.
e: Structural isomers have different bonding arrangements of atoms within the molecule.

q: All of the alkanes containing ____ or more carbon atoms show structural isomerism.
e: Butane ($C_4H_{10}$) is the smallest alkane that exhibits structural isomerism.

q: In the laboratory, alkanes are prepared by heating the sodium salt of a carboxylic acid with ____.
e: Decarboxylation using soda lime is a common laboratory method for preparing alkanes.

q: Soda lime is a mixture of ____ (lime) and sodium hydroxide.
e: Soda lime consists of calcium oxide and sodium hydroxide.

q: The reduction of alkyl halides with molecular hydrogen takes place in the presence of catalyst like platinum, Pt or ____, Pd.
e: Palladium and platinum are common catalysts for the reduction of alkyl halides to alkanes.

q: Although platinum and palladium metals in finely divided form catalyse the addition of hydrogen to alkenes at room temperature, higher temperatures are required when ____ is used as the hydrogenating catalyst.
e: Nickel requires higher temperatures compared to platinum or palladium for hydrogenation reactions.

q: The normal alkanes from $C_1$ to $C_4$ (i.e., from methane to butane) are colourless ____.
e: The first four straight-chain alkanes are gases at room temperature.

q: As the chain gets longer: melting and boiling points rise, ____ increases and flammability decreases.
e: Longer alkane chains have stronger intermolecular forces, leading to increased viscosity.

q: The most important chemical reactions of these saturated hydrocarbons are the substitution and ____ reactions.
e: Alkanes primarily undergo substitution and combustion reactions due to their saturated nature.

q: When methane is mixed with chlorine in ____ sunlight, the following stepwise reactions occur where one chlorine atom replaces one hydrogen atom in each step.
e: Halogenation of alkanes requires ultraviolet light, such as diffused sunlight, to initiate the reaction.

q: These reactions are known as ____ reactions in alkane.
e: The substitution of hydrogen by chlorine in an alkane is specifically called chlorination.

q: Haloalkanes such as $CH_2Cl_2$, $CHCl_3$ and $CCl_4$ are important ____.
e: Many haloalkanes are widely used as industrial and laboratory solvents.

q: The alkanes are ____ toward acids, bases, metals and many other chemicals.
e: Due to strong, non-polar C-C and C-H bonds, alkanes are generally unreactive.

q: Alkanes burn well in a good supply of oxygen, forming ____ and water vapour, and giving out plenty of heat.
e: Complete combustion of alkanes produces carbon dioxide and water.

q: If there is not enough oxygen, the alkanes undergo incomplete combustion, giving off poisonous ____ and less heat energy.
e: Incomplete combustion of alkanes yields toxic carbon monoxide gas.

q: Alkene molecules which are unsaturated hydrocarbons contain at least one carbon-carbon double bond (C=C) (____ bond).
e: The carbon-carbon double bond in alkenes is also referred to as an ethylenic bond.

q: They form a homologous series, with the general formula ____, where n is a number equal to or greater than 2.
e: The general formula for non-cyclic alkenes with one double bond is $C_nH_{2n}$.

q: The representative alkene given here is ____, $C_2H_4$.
e: Ethene is the simplest alkene, possessing the molecular formula $C_2H_4$.

q: The common name of ethene is ____.
e: Ethylene is the widely used common name for the IUPAC name ethene.

q: Identify and name the longest carbon chain containing the ____ bond.
e: In IUPAC nomenclature for alkenes, the parent chain must include the double bond.

q: Number the chain, starting at the end ____ to the double bond.
e: The carbon chain is numbered to give the double bond the lowest possible locant.

q: Number the first carbon of the double bond directly in front of the ____ name.
e: The position of the double bond is indicated by a number placed before the root name.

q: The first ____ members of the alkene family, ethene and propene, have only one structure but the higher members have more than one structure.
e: Ethene and propene cannot form structural isomers, unlike higher alkenes.

q: I and III or II and III are ____ isomers due to the different structures of C-skeleton in the longer chain.
e: Chain isomers differ in the arrangement of the carbon skeleton (straight vs. branched).

q: The basic carbon skeleton remains unchanged in the isomers I and II, but the double bonds are located in different positions, so I and II are ____ isomers.
e: Positional isomers have the same carbon skeleton but differ in the location of the functional group or double bond.

q: When ethanol is heated with concentrated sulphuric acid at ____ °C, ethene is formed.
e: Dehydration of ethanol to form ethene requires concentrated sulphuric acid at approximately 160 °C.

q: Ethene can be prepared from ethanol as a result of being passed over the heated ____, $Al_2O_3$.
e: Alumina ($Al_2O_3$) acts as a catalyst for the dehydration of alcohols to alkenes.

q: Passing the vapours of the alcohol over alumina, $Al_2O_3$, heated at ____ °C produces ethene.
e: The dehydration of ethanol over alumina catalyst is typically conducted at 350 °C.

q: The term ____ is used when a halogen atom and a hydrogen atom on an adjacent carbon of the same molecule are simultaneously removed as hydrogen halide.
e: Dehydrohalogenation is an elimination reaction that forms a double bond by removing HX.

q: When ethyl chloride is heated with an alcoholic solution of ____ on a water bath, ethene is formed.
e: Alcoholic potassium hydroxide (KOH) is a strong base used to promote dehydrohalogenation.

q: At room temperature, alkenes containing two to four carbon atoms are ____.
e: Lower molecular weight alkenes (C2 to C4) exist as gases at room temperature.

q: They burn in the air with a luminous, ____ flame.
e: Alkenes have a higher carbon-to-hydrogen ratio than alkanes, resulting in a smoky flame.

q: The unsaturated nature of alkenes (chemically reactive) is shown in the ____ reactions of alkenes.
e: The presence of the pi bond in alkenes makes them highly susceptible to addition reactions.

q: When hydrogen is added to ethene using suitable catalyst, ____ is the product.
e: Hydrogenation of ethene adds two hydrogen atoms across the double bond to yield ethane.

q: Halogens react with alkenes to produce ____ compounds.
e: Halogenation of an alkene results in the addition of two halogen atoms, forming a dihalogeno compound.

q: The addition of $Br_2$ to alkenes is used as a simple qualitative test for ____.
e: Bromine water decolorization is a standard test to detect the presence of unsaturation (double or triple bonds).

q: When an alkene is added, the reddish-brown solution becomes ____ as the $Br_2$ reacts with the alkene to form a colourless compound.
e: The reaction consumes the colored bromine, leaving a colourless dibromoalkane product.

q: This reaction provides the basis for ____ rule which may be stated as: When an unsymmetrical addendum (HX) adds on to an unsymmetrical alkene...
e: Markownikoff's rule predicts the major product in the electrophilic addition to unsymmetrical alkenes.

q: ...but that product where the negative part of the addendum adds on to the carbon with the ____ number of hydrogen atoms is the major product.
e: According to Markownikoff's rule, the electrophile adds to the carbon with more hydrogens, and the nucleophile to the carbon with fewer hydrogens.

q: When a stream of ____ oxygen is passed into a solution of alkene in glacial ethanoic acid (acetic acid) or chloroform, addition of ozone to alkene takes place...
e: Ozonolysis begins with the reaction of the alkene with ozonised oxygen to form an ozonide.

q: This ozonide is unstable and reduced with ____ and water to give aldehydes or ketones depending upon the structure of alkene.
e: Zinc dust is used to hydrolyze the ozonide and prevent further oxidation of the resulting aldehydes/ketones.

q: The complete process of preparing the ozonide followed by decomposing it, is called ____.
e: Ozonolysis is the cleavage of unsaturated bonds using ozone.

q: When ethene is passed into cold dilute ____ solution, ethene glycol is formed.
e: Hydroxylation of alkenes using cold, dilute potassium permanganate (Baeyer's reagent) yields diols like ethene glycol.

q: In this process, the colour of 1% dilute $KMnO_4$ solution is ____.
e: The purple colour of $KMnO_4$ is discharged (turns colourless/brown precipitate) as it oxidizes the alkene.

q: Alkyne molecules which are unsaturated hydrocarbons contain at least one carbon-carbon triple bond (C≡C) (____ bond).
e: The carbon-carbon triple bond characteristic of alkynes is known as an acetylenic bond.

q: The representative alkyne given here is ____, $C_2H_2$.
e: Ethyne is the simplest alkyne, containing two carbon atoms and the formula $C_2H_2$.

q: The first member of the series is known as ethyne, and it is commonly called ____.
e: Acetylene is the common industrial name for ethyne.

q: The suffix -ane of the alkane is replaced by ____.
e: In IUPAC nomenclature, the '-yne' suffix designates the presence of a carbon-carbon triple bond.

q: The chains with ____ or more carbon atoms lead to the formation of structural isomers in alkynes.
e: Butyne ($C_4H_6$) is the smallest alkyne capable of exhibiting structural isomerism.

q: ____ ($CaC_2$) reacts with water to produce acetylene.
e: The hydrolysis of calcium carbide is the standard laboratory and industrial method for generating acetylene.

q: The calcium carbide required for this reaction is industrially prepared by heating calcium oxide with ____ in an electric furnace.
e: Calcium oxide reacts with carbon (coke) at high temperatures to synthesize calcium carbide.

q: At room temperature, alkynes containing two to four carbon atoms are gases; those containing five to twelve are liquids; containing more than thirteen carbon atoms are ____.
e: Higher molecular weight alkynes exist as solids at room temperature due to stronger van der Waals forces.

q: They are all odourless and colourless except ethyne which has a slightly distinctive ____.
e: Pure ethyne is actually odourless, but commercial acetylene has a distinctive garlic-like odour due to impurities; the textbook notes it has a distinctive odour.

q: The reaction proceeds in ____ distinct stages when adding hydrogen to alkynes.
e: Hydrogenation of an alkyne first yields an alkene, and further hydrogenation yields an alkane.

q: Chlorine or bromine can be added to ethyne in the ____ to form ethyne di- and tetra-halides.
e: Halogenation of alkynes can occur via electrophilic addition even in the dark.

q: Iodine can be added to ethyne but only with ____.
e: Iodine is less reactive than chlorine or bromine, making its addition to alkynes difficult.

q: Addition of water to ethyne yields vinyl alcohol which tautomerizes to ____ (acetaldehyde).
e: The hydration of ethyne produces unstable vinyl alcohol, which rapidly rearranges to form ethanal.

q: The order of the readiness with which the hydrogen halides add to ethyne is ____.
e: The reactivity of hydrogen halides in addition reactions decreases from HI down to HF.

q: The addition reaction of vinyl bromide is in accordance with ____ rule.
e: Addition of HX to unsymmetrical alkenes or alkynes follows Markownikoff's rule.

q: When acetylene is passed over heated sodium, one or both hydrogen atoms may be replaced or substituted by sodium to form mono- and di-sodium ____.
e: Terminal alkynes are weakly acidic and react with alkali metals to form acetylide salts.

q: When ethyne is added to an ____ solution of copper(I) chloride or silver oxide, a precipitate is formed.
e: Ammoniacal solutions of copper(I) or silver(I) are used to test for terminal alkynes by forming explosive heavy metal acetylides.

q: $CH_3C \equiv CCH_3$ contains ____ on the triple bonded carbon and will not form metallic acetylides.
e: Only terminal alkynes possess an acidic hydrogen capable of being replaced by a metal to form an acetylide.

q: The alcohols may be considered as ____ of alkanes.
e: Alcohols are structurally derived from alkanes by substituting a hydrogen atom with a hydroxyl group.

q: The replacement of one hydrogen atom in an alkane by a ____ (-OH) group gives the corresponding alcohol.
e: The defining functional group of an alcohol is the hydroxyl (-OH) group.

q: They form a homologous series with the general formula ____ (or) $C_nH_{2n+2}O$ where n is a number equal to or greater than 1.
e: The general formula for aliphatic alcohols is commonly written as $C_nH_{2n+1}OH$ or $C_nH_{2n+2}O$.

q: The common name of an alcohol combines the name of the ____ group with the word alcohol.
e: Common names for alcohols are formed by stating the alkyl group name followed by the word 'alcohol'.

q: Alcohols are given their respective names by adding ____ instead of -ane of alkane.
e: In IUPAC nomenclature, the '-e' of the parent alkane is replaced by the suffix '-ol'.

q: Alcohols containing at least ____ carbon atoms have more than one structure.
e: Propanol ($C_3H_8O$) is the smallest alcohol that can exhibit positional isomerism.

q: Alcohols form ____ isomerism due to the different structures of C-skeleton in the longer chain.
e: Chain isomerism in alcohols occurs when the carbon skeleton can be arranged as straight or branched chains.

q: The basic carbon skeleton remains unchanged in the isomers, but a hydroxyl group (-OH) can be located in different positions, so they are ____ isomers.
e: Positional isomers of alcohols differ only in the carbon atom to which the -OH group is attached.

q: Ethene and steam are passed over a ____ catalyst at 570 °C and 60~70 atmospheric pressure to produce ethanol.
e: The industrial hydration of ethene to ethanol utilizes phosphoric acid as a catalyst.

q: ____ is used as the raw material for the preparation of ethanol industrially.
e: Starchy materials like maize and potatoes serve as the primary raw material for ethanol fermentation.

q: The cooked starch is cooled and then treated with freshly germinated barley which is called ____ for 1 hour at 60 °C.
e: Malt is germinated barley that provides the enzymes necessary to break down starch.

q: Malt contains the enzyme ____.
e: Diastase is the enzyme in malt responsible for hydrolyzing starch into maltose.

q: Starch breaks down into a sugar called ____.
e: The enzymatic action of diastase on starch yields the disaccharide maltose.

q: Yeast secretes two enzymes: (i) maltase which converts maltose into glucose and (ii) ____ which converts glucose into ethanol.
e: Zymase is the enzyme complex in yeast that catalyzes the anaerobic fermentation of glucose into ethanol and carbon dioxide.

q: The product contains about 11% ethanol and is fractionally distilled to yield the ____ spirit of commerce which contains about 95% ethanol.
e: Rectified spirit is the concentrated ethanol product obtained from the fractional distillation of fermented wash.

q: Alcohols from methanol, $CH_3OH$, to butanol, $C_4H_9OH$, are ____ liquids.
e: Lower molecular weight alcohols are colourless, mobile liquids with a characteristic odour.

q: The first two members; methanol and ethanol are ____ with water in any proportion.
e: Methanol and ethanol can form hydrogen bonds with water, making them completely miscible.

q: The most toxic member of the alcohol homologous series is ____.
e: Methanol is highly toxic and can cause blindness or death if ingested.

q: When a piece of sodium is added to ethanol, reaction occurs at room temperature, liberating ____.
e: Alcohols react with active metals like sodium to release hydrogen gas and form alkoxides.

q: With a smaller proportion of concentrated sulphuric acid, ____ is formed when the reaction temperature is kept at 140 °C.
e: Heating ethanol with excess sulphuric acid at 140 °C promotes intermolecular dehydration to form diethyl ether.

q: Ethanoic acid (acetic acid) also reacts with ethanol when a small amount of concentrated sulphuric acid is added as ____.
e: Concentrated sulphuric acid acts as an acid catalyst and dehydrating agent in esterification.

q: Ethyl ethanoate is an ester and it has a pleasant ____ odour which is a characteristic of most esters.
e: Esters are well-known for their sweet, fruity odours and are often used in flavourings.

q: When ethanol vapour is passed over freshly reduced copper heated at 300 °C, removal of hydrogen occurs with formation of ____ (also known as acetaldehyde).
e: Dehydrogenation of primary alcohols over heated copper yields aldehydes, such as ethanal from ethanol.

q: When ethanol is heated with acidified potassium dichromate solution, oxidation takes place in two stages to finally give ____.
e: Strong oxidizing agents like acidified potassium dichromate oxidize primary alcohols completely to carboxylic acids, yielding ethanoic acid.
